title: Theorem of the Day
summary: One theorem from quantum mechanics, quantum computing, or quantum information theory: its statement, a complete proof, and a new result we derive from it.

theorems.title: The no-cloning theorem
theorems.summary: No physical process can copy two distinct, non-orthogonal pure states. We prove it, then derive the exact fidelity tradeoff for approximately cloning two known states from N copies to M.
theorems.new_result: Geodesic tradeoff for cloning two pure states

references.title: A single quantum cannot be cloned
references.authors: W. K. Wootters, W. H. Zurek
references.note: The original no-cloning argument, from the linearity of quantum evolution.

references.title: Communication by EPR devices
references.note: An independent proof of no-cloning, made in the context of superluminal signalling.

references.title: Optimal universal and state-dependent quantum cloning
references.authors: D. Bruß, D. P. DiVincenzo, A. Ekert, C. A. Fuchs, C. Macchiavello, J. A. Smolin
references.note: Optimal 1 → 2 cloners, including the state-dependent cloner for two pure states.

references.title: Strategies and networks for state-dependent quantum cloning
references.note: Maximum global fidelity for N → M cloning of two pure states, including unequal prior probabilities. Our symmetric formula must agree with theirs.

references.title: Geometry of Quantum States
references.note: Book. Develops the Fubini–Study metric on pure states, whose triangle inequality drives the new proof.
